name: AI APIs and Integrations
blurb: Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, pricing, uptime, and changelogs for every public AI API.

reading.body:
AI APIs and Integrations is an index, not a dataset: it holds no entries of its own and points to four child pages covering API directory, pricing, status and uptime, and model serving providers.

The four child pages split the API surface into what exists, what it costs, whether it is up, and who runs it. The directory covers endpoints, SDKs, and authentication; pricing covers rates and rate limits; status covers reliability history and changelogs. Together they treat a public AI API as an operational system rather than a static catalog entry.

The model serving providers page is the only child that ties the API layer to physical infrastructure and governance. It lists 100+ providers with headquarters country and datacenter regions, and states that jurisdiction determines which AI regulations apply, including the EU AI Act, data residency, and export controls. Datacenter location therefore becomes a compliance variable, not just a latency or cost variable.

The hub itself contains no endpoints, prices, or status records, so it cannot show trends or incidents directly. The serving providers directory is sourced daily from the OpenRouter routing catalog, but the other child pages do not state their update frequency in this data.
